quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, press both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When braking:

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only on wet roads.
Always use both brakes.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: During a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
The motorcycle and rider lean in opposite directions.
Only the motorcycle leans, not the rider.
Only the rider leans, not the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider lean together.
questions.explanation: During normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can ride on the shoulder.
You can pass in a no-passing zone.
You must start and finish your pass in a passing zone.
You should honk to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish your pass in a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must be done only in areas where passing is safe and legal.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is not serious.
Takes away your ability to change direction.
Will fix itself automatically.
Is only a problem if the front tire also skids.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes away your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the wheel locks, you cannot change direction. You must release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Checking your motorcycle before riding:

options.text: Only works if a mechanic does it.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should only be done after a ride.
Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find any mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: Flash your brake light mainly when:

options.text: Passing another vehicle.
You need to slow down suddenly.
A stop sign is ahead.
Your turn signals don't work.

questions.correctAnswerText: You need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is smaller than a car's. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers notice when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, the best action is to:

options.text: Loosen your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the road's edge.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake gently on the good tire and steer to the road's edge.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep the motorcycle straight. Slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow, move to the road's edge, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting to first gear, you may need to:

options.text: Brake to slow down before downshifting safely.
Speed up before downshifting safely.
Swerve to the left.
Flash your brakes to warn drivers behind you about downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake to slow down before downshifting safely.
questions.explanation: Slow down before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting at high speed can make the motorcycle jerk and cause the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: What color and lettering does a warning sign have?

options.text: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
Blue with white lettering or symbols.
Red with white lettering or symbols.
White with black lettering or symbols.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering or symbols.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following gives a rider the best protection?

options.text: Goggles
A face shield
A windshield
Eyeglasses

questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face if you crash. Goggles protect your eyes only. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If your friend has been drinking alcohol, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Arrange for a safe ride home for your friend.
Keep your friend busy with activities.
Keep your friend from leaving until they are sober.
Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow your friend to ride their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Never let an impaired friend ride a motorcycle. Instead, arrange another way for them to get home, keep them busy with other activities, and do not let them leave until they are sober. Ask other friends to help stop them.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the rear brake first.
Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes together. Brake firmly and do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
Let several riders pass the vehicle at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to show no other motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider finish passing before the next rider starts to pass.
questions.explanation: Riders in a group should pass one at a time. Each rider should complete their pass and return to formation before the next rider begins to pass.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Sit with your arms holding you up rather than steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced in turns. Your arms should steer, not hold you up. Sit close enough that your arms bend slightly when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: Riders who do not wear helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who do wear helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries during a crash than riders who wear helmets.

questions.question: A rectangular sign is usually a:

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: You should choose a lane position that:

options.text: Reduces your space cushion and lets others see you.
Increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
Increases road hazards you encounter and lets others pass you.
Reduces road hazards and lets you follow another vehicle closely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases your space cushion and lets others see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that increases your space cushion. This helps you see others and lets them see you. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good position discourages others from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the:

options.text: Motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
Motorcycle could speed up too quickly.
Front tire will likely skid.
Engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle could jerk and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear tire may skid.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first.
Reduce speed and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, apply both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.question: How should you lean a motorcycle when turning?

options.text: Always press the left handgrip.
Always press the right handgrip.
Press the handgrip opposite the direction you are turning.
Press the handgrip in the direction you are turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you are turning.
questions.explanation: To turn a motorcycle, it must lean. Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn to make the motorcycle lean.

questions.question: What should boots or shoes do to protect a rider?

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Have long laces that hang loose.
Cover the ankle and provide support.
Have tall heels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Wear tall, sturdy boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they do not catch on anything. Tuck in long laces so they do not get caught in the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist tell a passenger to do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Hold onto the seat.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after you start the engine.
questions.explanation: Give your passenger safety instructions before riding. Have them get on the motorcycle only after the engine is started. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Where do motorcycle operators and other drivers most often have conflicts?

options.text: At intersections
On highways
On rural roads
In parking lots

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk of conflict between motorcyclists and other drivers. Riders should be extra careful at intersections.
